text: This gives the parallel process — the informal one, running underneath the four documented steps — with specific actors, specific failure points, and no diagram in sight: the porter who never reads the substitution line, the sous chef's verbal aside, "ask the kitchen" standing in for a documented specials line, the ticket note binned at close, the spreadsheet updated from memory off-site, two sites running different laminates, the manager hunting email while the EHO waits. That's the territory, not the map.

params.wrong_if: The substitution line on a delivery note is in fact read and acted on before service, or the two sites' printed matrices are shown to match on any given day.

text: Filed as seq 3, stakeholder level, parent seq 2, flagged no-evidence.

Seven bets, each stated so it could fail — capture must happen at the porter's signature not the chef's re-entry, spec-sheet reading has to beat chef memory, the remainder-entry has to take under a minute, the import has to be one-off not a re-key, the reprint has to be automatic, the owner has to value the record over the matrix, and the EHO/insurer have to accept it as evidence before, not after, it's built. None of these is already true today by your own account in a2 and a3, and you've ordered them for testing. That's a named bet, not a checklist.

params.wrong_if: A porter-signed substitution capture is tried and chefs still re-enter it themselves, or the EHO/insurer decline to commit to accepting the record as evidence before it's built.

text: Filed as seq 4, solution level, parent seq 3, flagged no-evidence.

This isolates one variable — capture at the delivery note — and explains why it's load-bearing (everything downstream just redescribes an already-wrong matrix if it fails), then gives a single test: two sites, four weeks, porters photographing notes, checked against the wholesaler's own log, with an explicit threshold (under 80%) and an explicit consequence (the capture point moves off the porter). It also shows the other six conditions are cheaper and separable, rather than bundling everything into one round of interviews.

params.wrong_if: The two-site, four-week test is run and porter-captured substitutions match the wholesaler's log at 80% or above, yet the capture point is moved off the porter anyway, or is left in place after falling below 80%.

text: Filed as seq 5, transition level, parent seq 4, flagged no-evidence.

This names four distinct roles with different relationships to pain and money — head chef (daily operational pain, no budget), waiter (moment-of-truth pain, no budget), diner (carries the risk, isn't even a customer), owner/ops director (holds the budget, feels nothing until the EHO or solicitor calls) — plus a possible fifth, the insurance broker, flagged as needing one conversation before pricing. It goes further than naming the split: it draws the design consequence from it (capture must cost the chef nothing; the sale is liability cover to the owner, not convenience to the kitchen). That's well past a single persona.

params.wrong_if: The owner or ops director turns out to be willing to pay for chef-facing convenience alone, without the liability-record framing, or the broker conversation shows the broker has no influence on the purchase.

text: Filed as seq 6, stakeholder level, parent seq 1, flagged no-evidence.

This answers all three parts as posed, not as an estimate: not a quick fix (explicitly distinguished from the spreadsheet-template fix that already failed twice), a big idea scoped to one six-week cycle with a fixed team and an explicit cut order under time pressure — spec-sheet automation degrades first, the timestamped record is protected last because that's what the owner is paying for, per seq 6 — and no redesign of EPOS or costing, with the redesign question answered by naming what would count as losing (asking a chef to re-key a menu). Appetite is treated as an input constraining scope, not a duration guessed from the work.

params.wrong_if: The cycle runs past six weeks and the cut falls on the timestamped record rather than spec-sheet automation, or the EPOS/costing systems end up being modified to fit the new tool.

text: Filed as seq 7, solution level, parent seq 6, flagged no-evidence.

This works through all four framing questions with specifics rather than deferral: new work is isolated precisely (reading a wet, handwritten, folded note — not the PDF work you already know), the unnamed fitting-together assumption is named (the matching layer between supplier product names, recipe ingredients, and costing-system names) and correctly flagged as needing a spike before the cycle rather than during it, two unbuilt design solutions are flagged as unproven rather than assumed easy (sub-minute special entry, the mid-service screen), and two hard decisions are settled in advance with their consequences stated ("may contain" folded into "contains" because it changes the data model; a porter's photo marks dishes "unverified" rather than waiting silently, else condition one collapses back onto the chef). Nothing here is left for the build to sort out.

params.wrong_if: The matching-layer spike is skipped and the cycle proceeds anyway, or a porter's photo is built to wait silently for chef confirmation rather than marking dishes unverified.

text: Filed as seq 8, transition level, parent seq 7, flagged no-evidence.

This lists concrete, specific exclusions rather than leaving scope to be cut later under pressure: automatic spec-sheet reading deferred to a later cycle contingent on capture holding, the wholesaler feed kept manual until three real formats are seen, no diner-facing surface (with the reason given — liability shifts, and that conversation with the insurer hasn't happened), EPOS/costing as import-only forever, Natasha's Law and nutrition explicitly named and declined, single-group scope, and one permanent boundary distinguishing "records what's confirmed" from "tells the diner it's safe". Each exclusion is tied to a reason, not just asserted.

params.wrong_if: The product ships anything diner-facing or a QR allergen menu within this cycle, or it writes back into the EPOS or costing system rather than only importing from them.

text: Filed as seq 9, solution level, parent seq 6, flagged no-evidence.

This names who is accountable in law (unchanged: the food business operator) and who absorbs it in practice today (waiter and chef, not the porter who actually signed the substitution) — then states plainly that the design shifts the practical picture rather than pretending it doesn't, with three concrete, testable commitments: the system asserts "recorded and confirmed by whom," never "safe"; accountability covers record fidelity, not chef correctness; and the ledger is immutable to everyone including the owner, with the reason given (editable history stops being evidence and becomes a blame weapon). That's a stated accountability structure with consequences, not a flag.

params.wrong_if: The owner, or anyone else, is able to alter or delete a ledger entry after the fact, or the system at any point asserts a dish is "safe" rather than what was recorded and confirmed.

text: Filed as seq 10, solution level, parent seq 6, flagged no-evidence.

Four dated stop-conditions and one dateless one, each describing a result that could genuinely happen and be observed: capture below 80% even after moving the point off the porter, a laminate reverting to spreadsheet printing at either site, fewer than three of five owners willing to pay or the broker saying it moves nothing, an EHO rejecting a digital ledger in writing, and a wrong record surfacing at a diner reaction. Each has a named metric, most have a date, and each says what stopping means in that case rather than gesturing at "monitoring results."

params.wrong_if: Capture stays under 80% past the end of October, or a laminate reverts to spreadsheet printing after the ship date, and the cycle continues anyway without being stopped.

text: Filed as seq 11, transition level, parent seq 4, flagged no-evidence.

This gives, per model step, a domain-specific set built from real artefacts (your own spec sheets including the awkward multi-page scanned ones, real delivery photos from the capture test, the flagship menu's actual product-to-ingredient pairs), a named owner whose judgement is being stood in for and who runs it rather than delegating to engineering, and pass rates that are asymmetric and justified rather than a single flat number — zero tolerance on missed "contains" because that failure mode is a diner, five percent tolerance on false positives because that failure mode is one chef confirmation, ninety-five percent on matching with unmatched lines surfaced rather than silently dropped. It also names the double-labelling by two head chefs as the ceiling on what "correct" can mean, and states the eval runs on the whole pipeline, re-run on every supplier or model change, reported monthly to the person whose name is on the record.

params.wrong_if: A release ships with even one missed "contains" on the eval set, or the eval is run and reported by engineering rather than the flagship head chef.

text: Filed as seq 12, solution level, parent seq 3, flagged no-evidence.

text: This answers all five parts of the cascade with the specificity the weak-answer note asks for: the aspiration is a provable state of the world, not a revenue figure; where-to-play excludes single sites and big chains and QSR by name, each with a stated reason; how-we-win is a real mechanism — sell the record to the owner rather than the matrix to the chef, fed by the porter so it costs the kitchen nothing, non-editable so it counts as evidence, reaching the owner through the broker — not a list of features; capabilities are named concretely (photo-reading, the matching layer, an append-only ledger, wholesaler and broker relationships); and management systems name an actual operating number, an eval cadence and owner, kill dates reviewed on the day they fall, and an editability rule enforced in code rather than policy.

params.wrong_if: The product is sold or adopted primarily on chef convenience rather than owner-facing liability evidence, or a single-site or large-chain group becomes a target account.

This produces exactly the kind of specific, awkward failure the premortem asks for, not a vague adoption worry: capture passes under observation (a Hawthorne effect) then quietly halves when a porter leaves and nobody notices because the reported number was monthly and self-reported by the chef; confirmation degrades into a one-click Monday ritual that clears flags without opening them, so the ledger looks clean while being empty; front-of-house trust in the laminate rises faster than the ledger's actual truth, so the old verbal check disappears; the ledger that was sold as protection becomes the first exhibit against the chef and the second against the owner; the broker conversation that was never put in writing turns out to matter; and the team is shown building the very thing it had declared out of bounds in a9, "because it was the interesting problem." That last line alone is the kind of sentence a real premortem produces and a hedge never does.

params.wrong_if: Capture-rate reporting relies on self-reported monthly figures without independent spot-checks, or a confirmation is implemented as a single click that does not require opening the underlying change.

text: Filed as seq 14, transition level, parent seq 9, flagged no-evidence.

That's a real alternative space, not a feature relabelled as a need.

params.wrong_if: Fewer than three of five owners agree to pay and no conversation with a wholesaler about the portal-flag alternative follows.

text: This is entirely retrospective and evidentiary, exactly as asked: a specific Tuesday in March, a named WhatsApp thread with an actual message and a two-thumbs-up non-response, a file with a literal "v7 FINAL (2).xlsx" name sitting two versions ahead of the laminate on the wall, a spec sheet located only by searching "spec" and scrolling, the actual tab open on a manager's laptop during a real inspection, and the real eleven-day gap between the substitution and the sheet being rebuilt. Nothing here is conditional — it's what was done, found, and left undone, with the artefacts named.

params.wrong_if: A comparable substitution record can in fact be found outside the WhatsApp thread, or the laminate on the wall matches the head chef's spreadsheet version at the time of the next inspection.

This stays on the timeline throughout: a specific Thursday in June, a specific site, a specific dish and diner, the stale v6 laminate, a save that traces back to one man's memory of a WhatsApp photo from three months prior, the manager's retelling as a good-news story, and then the pivot — driving over, asking what was true about that dish that night, finding nobody could answer, and the broker's question the next morning landing with no answer behind it. That's a dated, sensory account of the specific moment realisation happened, not a general preference.

params.wrong_if: A record of what was true about that specific dish on that Thursday can in fact be produced after the fact, or the near-miss did not actually change what was done afterwards.

text: Filed as seq 17, stakeholder level, parent seq 1, flagged no-evidence.

This names three specific, dated shifts rather than gesturing at "AI": phone-photo and footnoted-PDF reading dropping to a cost where it can be checked rather than hand-typed, closing the gap that killed the two abandoned tools; the post-2021 change in enforcement posture (Natasha's Law and the prosecutions that followed) turning allergens into an owner's personal fear and something brokers now ask about at renewal; and wholesalers' pandemic-era digitisation putting the substitution log into data form even where it's still only printed. It also states the counter-case honestly — that the vacuum might persist because restaurants don't pay for software — rather than only arguing the favourable side, and ties that directly back to the kill-date and pivot decisions already on record.

params.wrong_if: Photo and PDF reading still requires hand-typed correction at a rate that puts the chef back in the loop, or brokers turn out not to ask about allergen records at renewal.

This pairs each exclusion with a specific named person and a specific reason they're annoyed — the marketing manager wanting the QR menu, the single-site chef who can't pay, the sales lead wanting a chain-compliance logo, the ops director wanting one tool for everything, the investor wanting a "safe" demo, the chef experiencing this as done-to-them, and the account manager who can see the upside faster than you're moving. And it does the harder thing the note is checking for: it names the one annoyance — the owner wanting to tidy the ledger — that must never be resolved, distinguishing a permanent boundary from a "later."

params.wrong_if: The owner is granted any mechanism to edit or annotate past ledger entries, or a diner-facing feature ships before the liability conversation with the insurer has happened.

text: Filed as seq 19, solution level, parent seq 6, flagged no-evidence.

This has a genuine customer-facing headline and benefit ("show what was in any dish on any day"), no internal vocabulary — no "capture rate," "ledger," or "matching layer" anywhere in it — a concrete before/after mechanism written in plain language, a quote from a named persona that echoes the actual switch moment (the chef's memory being the only thing standing between a diner and a mistake), and a real getting-started path with a real price. It reads like something rewritten toward a customer, not a feature list dressed up.

params.wrong_if: A pilot owner reads this and cannot say what "one tap" would actually show them, or the porter-to-floor marking takes materially longer than "minutes" in practice.

text: Filed as seq 20, solution level, parent seq 17, flagged no-evidence.

This is the one place explicitly checking for the failure the weak-answer note names, and it doesn't fall into it: value is split correctly between buyer and three distinct users with different adoption postures; usability names three specific undesigned moments rather than asserting design is easy; feasibility separates the boring known work from the real risk (matching, bad photographs) and sequences the spike accordingly; and viability goes past "it's a viable business" into what viability actually costs you — long-term retention and cross-group visibility as your own new liability, and the need for your own cover before the first site goes live, since an unfaithful record puts you in the witness box too.

params.wrong_if: The matching-layer spike does not run before the six-week spine build starts, or the company goes live at a first site without its own liability cover in place.

text: Filed as seq 21, transition level, parent seq 7, flagged no-evidence.

The default is unambiguous: no extension, cooldown, and the scope-cutting order already agreed applies before it ever gets to that point. The one exception is stated in advance, narrowly scoped, and capped (one site waiting only on menu import, two weeks, cooldown only) precisely so it can't be argued open-endedly on the day. And it draws the harder distinction correctly: a missing matching layer isn't an extension case at all, it's a wrong spike, reshaped and re-pitched rather than stretched. The value sits in the default, exactly as the question asks.

params.wrong_if: The cycle is extended past six weeks for a reason other than the single named menu-import exception, or that exception runs longer than two weeks in cooldown.

text: Filed as seq 22, transition level, parent seq 7, flagged no-evidence.

text: This names every incumbent artefact individually and states precisely how each coexists rather than assuming a clean cutover: the laminate stays and gets printed by you, the binder stays for the inspector with a monthly extract, the costing system stays master-of-dishes with one-way import, the EPOS field is declared in writing not-the-record rather than fixed, WhatsApp is left alone. It identifies the real two-year risk correctly (two truths on two walls, not "dual entry kills adoption" in the abstract) and gives the actual mechanism meant to resolve it — a policy naming the system of record, a version stamp, and a monthly check that will show whether it's holding, rather than assuming coexistence quietly disappears.

params.wrong_if: An unstamped laminate is found on a wall at a monthly check and no action follows, or the EPOS allergen field is ever treated as authoritative in a dispute.

text: Filed as seq 26, transition level, parent seq 25, flagged no-evidence.

This gives a specific date and a specific, conjunctive state, not a review: five measured numbers — twenty full-price groups, capture above eighty percent measured against the wholesaler's own log rather than self-reported, verified days above ninety percent, one broker's written policy commitment, and zero instances of ledger unfaithfulness — all five required, with the consequence stated as fact (the product stops) rather than a prompt to reconsider. It also names a second, independent date and consequence for the wholesaler pivot, so there's no room for a turnaround story to substitute for the numbers.

params.wrong_if: On 30 June 2027 fewer than all five conditions are met and the restaurant product continues anyway, or the September 2027 wholesaler pilot deadline passes without closure being enacted.

text: Filed as seq 27, transition level, parent seq 23, flagged no-evidence.

This answers the actual detector question precisely rather than settling for "yes": it identifies which metric is a trap and how (verified days climbing via the Monday-click while the wall stays wrong — the premortem recurring as a number) and states the specific design fix (confirmation only counts if the change was opened; report time-to-confirm as a distribution, not an average, so a Monday spike is visible as a spike). It checks capture rate against the same test and finds it clean by construction, but still flags the secondary drift risk (fewer substitutions making the number look better for the wrong reason) by pairing it with an absolute count. And it names the real vanity metric — days since an incident — states plainly that it satisfies the test perfectly, and commits to never showing it, with the switch-story detail making the point rather than just asserting it.

params.wrong_if: A confirmation is counted as valid without the underlying change having been opened, or "days since an incident" appears on any owner-facing screen.

text: Filed as seq 28, transition level, parent seq 23, flagged no-evidence.

This gets the ordering exactly right rather than defaulting to "try again": it names four distinct failure modes and states which are visible and on what timescale (false positive visible within the hour, false negative invisible for months, match failure and unreadable photos silently invisible), draws the design consequence from that asymmetry (surface unmatched lines rather than dropping them, bounce unreadable photos back immediately, run a weekly second-chef spot-check as the only catch for a missed "contains" before a diner does), and states who actually pays in order — diner with their body, waiter and chef with their jobs, owner in court, you in the witness box — with the explicit point that design changes the queue length, not who's in it.

params.wrong_if: An unreadable delivery-note photo is silently dropped rather than bounced back to the porter, or the weekly second-chef spot-check is skipped for a period and nobody notices.

text: Filed as seq 29, solution level, parent seq 6, flagged no-evidence.

This names each piece of evidence by type rather than asserting confidence: one anecdote, process evidence that isn't demand evidence, evidence against a rival design rather than for this one, a self-interested data point explicitly excluded from counting, and explicit zeros for owner interviews, brokers, inspectors, and capture data. It then makes the proportionality judgement the question actually asks for, not just once but calibrated to two different decisions: thin evidence is enough to justify the cheap learning spend already committed, but not enough to justify shipping a self-printing sheet a waiter will trust more than the old one — and it names the specific different kind of evidence shipping would require (zero-miss eval, pre-print chef confirmation, weekly spot-check), rather than treating "more evidence" as one undifferentiated pile.

params.wrong_if: A self-printing sheet goes live at a site before the zero-missed-contains eval, pre-print chef confirmation, and weekly spot-check are all in place.
